decisions.decision: Use BORE scheduler patch (firelzrd/bore-scheduler v6.6.3 for 6.18.22)
decisions.rationale: BORE extends EEVDF with burst-awareness — gaming tasks (short bursts) get scheduling priority over batch tasks. Upstream EEVDF alone doesn't distinguish interactive from batch.
1ms tick granularity allows scheduler decisions every 1ms. At HZ=250 (4ms), frame pacing inconsistencies emerge below 250fps. Gaming at 60-165Hz requires sub-4ms scheduling.
Full preemption allows the scheduler to preempt any kernel code not holding a spinlock. This directly reduces wake latency and input latency.
THP=always causes background memory compaction which creates stutters. THP=madvise lets game engines request hugepages explicitly without background compaction overhead.

decisions.decision: BBR TCP congestion control as default
decisions.rationale: BBR optimizes for bandwidth and latency simultaneously. Better for online gaming than CUBIC (which sacrifices latency for throughput).
BFQ provides fair queue bandwidth and low latency for interactive processes. Prevents background downloads from blocking game asset loading.
alternatives_rejected: deadline (good for NVMe but no fairness)

decisions.rationale: Wine/Proton translate Windows sync objects. NTSync provides native kernel support, eliminating emulation overhead. Merged upstream in 6.14.
MGLRU better tracks memory access patterns across generations. Reduces reclaim-induced stutters during gaming by keeping recently-used game assets warm.
Both patches modify the same scheduler files. Using bore-cachy on top of bore-scheduler would cause conflicts. bore-scheduler is sufficient and clean.
decisions.proof: 3/25 hunks FAILED in dry-run when applied over bore-scheduler

decisions.decision: O2 + pipe (not O3 + march=native for now)
decisions.rationale: O3 can introduce subtle bugs in kernel code. For v1.0, O2 is the safe choice. O3+native can be enabled in EXPERIMENTAL profile after validation.
